text: Sabrina is a British goddess or folkloric figure. A goddess of that name guarded the River Severn. Many Celtic goddesses lived in a river and its watershed. Evidence from Britain and the continent supports this reading. Sabrina also survived as a character in tale. The English poet John Milton put her in his Masque of Comus. Milton drew on the story of Locrine, king of Loegria. The invader Humber defeated Locrine. Humber hid his love Estrildis in a chamber underground. There she bore his child, Sabrina. Humber was already married to Gwendolen, princess of Cornwall. When her father died, Gwendolen marched against Humber and won. She ordered Estrildis and Sabrina drowned in the Severn. The tale paints Sabrina as the spirit of that river.
